title_ne: रामराजा प्रसाद सिंह स्वास्थ्य विज्ञान प्रतिष्‍ठान ऐन, २०८३
summary:
The name of this bill is the "Ramraja Prasad Singh Academy of Health Sciences Act, 2083" (Section 1, Subsection 1, Page 1). The main purpose of this bill is to prepare the skilled human resources required for the country through high-level study, teaching, and research in the field of health sciences, and to provide accessible, affordable, and quality health services to the general public (Preamble, Page 1; Section 3, Subsection 1, Page 2). This Act shall come into force immediately (Section 1, Subsection 2, Page 1).

The Academy must maintain contact with the Nepal Government through the Ministry responsible for health matters of the Nepal Government (Section 41, Page 16). The Assembly shall provide necessary suggestions to the Nepal Government during the formulation of national health and education policies (Section 9, Clause j, Page 6). The Executive Council shall coordinate as necessary with provincial governments, local levels, and the private sector (Section 12, Subsection 1, Clause j, Page 7). Money received from the Nepal Government, provincial governments, and local levels shall be deposited in the fund of the Academy (Section 32, Subsection 2, Clause a, Page 15). If the Academy cannot be operated for any reason, the Nepal Government may dissolve the Academy on the recommendation of the Assembly (Section 42, Subsection 1, Page 16). Upon dissolution of the Academy, its movable and immovable assets and liabilities shall belong to the Nepal Government (Section 42, Subsection 2, Page 16).

Permanent employees of the Nepal Health Service working in Gajendra Narayan Singh Hospital at the commencement of this Act who wish to work in the Academy must submit an application to the Ministry within 6 months from the date of commencement of the regulations relating to employee administration (Section 31, Subsection 1, Page 15). The Academy must submit an annual report of the work performed by it in that fiscal year to the Assembly through the Vice-Chancellor within 3 months after the end of each fiscal year (Section 43, Subsection 1, Page 17). The Academy must obtain the approval of the Nepal Government, Ministry of Finance before performing any work or making any decision that creates financial liability on the Nepal Government (Section 44, Page 17). The Assembly must obtain the approval of the Nepal Government, Ministry of Finance when making rules or regulations that create a financial burden on the Nepal Government (Section 46, Subsection 3, Page 18; Section 47, Subsection 2, Page 18). Nominated or appointed office bearers of the Academy who have a direct or indirect interest, concern, or conflict of interest in matters related to the interest or concern of the Academy must self-declare it and remain separate from the decision-making process (Section 34, Page 16). A person appointed or nominated to the post of office bearer must take an oath before assuming the charge of their post (Section 45, Page 17). The Academy shall not grant affiliation or approval to any educational institution other than its own educational institution (Section 36, Page 16).

Students, trainees, or researchers pursuing higher education from the Academy shall be awarded degrees and certificates as approved by the Assembly, and honorary degrees may be conferred on persons performing commendable work in research and academic fields (Section 35, Subsections 1 and 2, Page 16). The Academic Council shall determine the standard of study, research, training, and instruction programs operated by the Academy, determine examination standards, conduct examinations, and publish results (Section 14, Clauses e and h, Page 9). Provisions regarding the determination of seat numbers, reservation, entrance examination, student admission, tuition fees, and scholarships for medical education studies shall be in accordance with prevailing laws on medical education (Section 38, Page 16). The Academy shall not give affiliation or approval to any educational institution other than its own educational institution (Section 36, Page 16).

This bill establishes the Ramraja Prasad Singh Academy of Health Sciences as an autonomous body corporate with perpetual succession, with its central office located in Rajbiraj Municipality of Saptari District (Section 3, Subsections 1 and 2, Page 2; Section 4, Subsection 1, Page 2). The main functions of the Academy are to conduct or cause to be conducted study, teaching, training, and research in various health-related subjects, produce skilled human resources for quality health services, provide quality and accessible health services to the general public, organize seminars and health camps, and publish textbooks (Section 7, Subsection 1, Page 3). As the supreme body of the Academy, an Assembly shall be constituted with the Prime Minister as Chancellor and the Registrar as member-secretary (Section 8, Subsections 1 and 2, Pages 3-5). An Executive Council chaired by the Vice-Chancellor shall serve as the executive body of the Academy (Section 11, Subsections 1 and 2, Pages 6-7). The Vice-Chancellor shall be the whole-time chief office bearer of the Academy, whose term of office shall be 4 years and who may be reappointed once (Section 19, Subsections 1 and 2, Page 10). The Academy shall have a separate fund containing money received from the Nepal Government, provincial governments, local levels, study/service fees, domestic or foreign persons, governments, or organizations, and the money of this fund shall be deposited by opening an account in a Class 'A' commercial bank, while the final audit of the Academy shall be conducted by the Auditor General (Section 32, Subsections 1, 2, and 4, Page 15; Section 33, Subsection 4, Page 15).
